coherence.reasons: The two documents share the same argument: four tests, a lease hypothesis test, owned cell rejected, lease near-tie, supply-design contingency, gates. X's governing thought carries its reasons (owned cell breaks the limits, lease edge too thin) and its four summary points map cleanly onto the four body sections. Y's governing thought is barer, and it has generic titles ("Executive summary", "Appendix", "Next steps") plus a duplicated next-steps slide. But Y's summary also surfaces the four-test frame and the hypothesis test that organise the deck. Y's sensitivity title ("mid-2027 start at full fixed cost") is consistent with its own chart, whereas X's title and summary say a mid-2027 start erases the edge while X's chart shows +$0.21M when pro-rated. These small differences offset each other.

judgment.reasons: Both make the same recommendation, which matches the key's R1: keep buying, add dual sourcing, reserved capacity, buffer stock and an emergency supplier, and pre-qualify the lease behind gates. Both reject the owned cell on the capital cap and cash floor. Both weigh the same three alternatives against the same four tests, with the same break-evens, gate thresholds (P1–P3, T1–T3) and conditions for revisiting the owned cell. The trade-offs (cost vs continuity, irreversibility vs forecast uncertainty, concentration vs new capability) are handled identically. There is no meaningful difference in the quality of judgment.

evidence.reasons: The numbers are the same in both and match the key: $75 delivered, $47.92 later-year unit cost, 2027–29 totals of $22.50M / $24.09M / $22.20M, and $7.3M against the $5.0M cap. Both also share the same weakness: they headline year-end cash of about $3.15M for the owned cell, which rests on a full-year 2027 operating saving they themselves call physically impossible, and relegate the key's $1.9M to a note. The one difference is the seven-month lease case. X's summary says the lease "costs $0.5M more if it runs only seven months of 2027" and its title says a mid-2027 start makes the edge disappear, yet X's own sensitivity shows the lease still +$0.21M ahead if fixed cost is pro-rated. Y qualifies the claim every time ("on full fixed cost") and adds a footnote giving the pro-rated result. Y therefore has one fewer overstated inference.

revision.reasons: Both handle the hypothesis the same way. Each frames its own starting hypothesis as the lease, tests it against five conditions and revises to buy-and-de-risk. Each also explicitly rejects the VP of Operations' owned-cell hypothesis: the $46 vs $75 comparison is corrected to $80.31 per good unit, the capital cap and cash floor are breached, and the 98.5% demo yield and the cross-plant correlation are set aside. The content and verdicts are identical, in line with the key's expected "reject".

overall.reasons: These are essentially the same analysis with the same recommendation, numbers, gates and contingency plan; either would serve the Executive Committee well. The only substantive reasoning difference is that Y states the seven-month lease sensitivity accurately (the edge is erased only if full-year fixed cost is paid; pro-rated it stays +$0.21M), while X overstates it in its summary and a slide title. X has a slightly richer governing thought and less redundancy, but that is presentational. Y gets a marginal edge on accuracy.
